Yes: Pulu was his Babylonian name
R. W. Rogers (1912), p. 308; the site's person data

Rogers writes that the new king “was proclaimed under the name and style of Tiglathpileser in Assyria, and later under the name of Pulu in Babylonia”. The site's person data files 2 Kings 15:19 under Tiglath-pileser.[15]
The KJV wording reads as two kings

The KJV of 1 Chronicles 5:26 has “the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried them away” — two names, one verb in the singular. 1 Chronicles 5:26
Scripture gives no age, mother or burial for Menahem.
Kings does not give the year of his reign in which Pul came.
From the textPul, who came against the land in his reign (2 Kings 15:19), is identified with Tiglath-pileser III; see the question below.
